Opened #47641 for this.

One concrete source is zen itself: an exhausted free tier returns 429 with `retry-after` set to the seconds left until the next daily reset (`getRetryAfterDay` in `packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/ipRateLimiter.ts`), and `SessionRetry.delay()` honors that header up to `RETRY_MAX_DELAY`, so the session parks on a single attempt that can be up to 24h out. Nothing is logged after the first `stream error`, and inside a subagent even the retry status is invisible because it is published on the child session ID.

The PR stops the schedule when the requested wait is longer than 5 minutes, after publishing the retry status so the free tier and Go limit dialogs still fire. Short rate limits keep the current behavior.

Independent reproduction on **1.18.20** (release build, macOS 26 arm64), with two datapoints the thread may find useful: a measurement of what the flip costs on a local prefix-cached backend, and a workaround that made the prompt byte-stable.

**Setup:** ~20 skills present as physical copies in both `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` (Claude Code and Codex each read only their own root, so both copies have to exist). Also the `superpowers` plugin, whose package ships `brainstorming` and `systematic-debugging`, which also exist in both roots.

**Method:** pointed the provider `baseURL` at a tiny local HTTP server that dumps the request body, ran `opencode run --agent <custom> "selam"` three times per configuration, diffed the captured system prompts.

| configuration | 3 consecutive starts byte-identical? |
|---|---|
| default (both roots + plugin) | no – every `<location>` flips between `.claude` and `.agents` |
| `~/.agents/skills` symlinked to `~/.claude/skills` | no – same flips, path text differs |
| only the 2 plugin-duplicated skills removed from `~/.agents` | no – remaining 18 still flip; the 2 now flip between `~/.claude` and the plugin package |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1` + `~/.config/opencode/skills` = symlinks to `~/.claude/skills/*` | no – the 2 plugin-duplicated skills still flip between the single root and the package |
| same, but the 2 plugin-provided skills excluded from the single root | **yes** |

So the race is not limited to the `~/.claude` vs `~/.agents` pair; a plugin package that ships a skill of the same name races with a single configured root too.

**Cost, measured on a local backend with a persistent prefix cache (oMLX, 2048-token blocks):** the first divergent `<location>` lands around token ~6.1–8k of a 13.4k-token prompt, so a fresh session reuses only the first 3 blocks (tool definitions) and re-prefills the remaining ~7k tokens every start. On a 27B model on an M5 laptop that is ~30 s of extra prefill per new session that would otherwise be a cache hit. In-session turns are unaffected. For cloud providers this is the "one cache miss per restart" already described above, but for slow local backends it is a noticeable wall-clock penalty.

**Workaround** for anyone needing the exact bytes stable today: `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1`, a single `~/.config/opencode/skills` root built from per-skill symlinks, and leaving out any skill that a plugin already provides. Deterministic precedence in `add()` (or sorting the scan results before dedup, as #32203 proposed) would make this unnecessary.

Another instance of the same root cause, different MCP server: `substack-mcp`'s `set_post_body` tool publishes a ProseMirror-style document schema (packages/substack-mcp/src/api/substack/document.js) where `listItemNode` and `bulletListNode`/`orderedListNode` reference each other via getters — a genuine mutual recursion that zod-to-json-schema turns into a $ref cycle. Same symptoms as this issue: fails on the very first message, even with the plain `build` agent and no other plugins/MCPs enabled, as soon as `substack` MCP is configured and model is `muse-spark-1.2/1.3-contributor-free` via Console. Workaround that worked for me: `"permission": {"substack_set_post_body": "deny"}` in opencode.jsonc, which drops just that one tool and leaves the rest of the MCP working. +1 for fixing this generally in the schema transform layer rather than per-MCP-server, since it's clearly not limited to postgres/houseCARL/substack — any tool with a tree-shaped schema will hit it.

Hey everyone, wanted to share how I finally got the desktop app working on Windows 11 after running into the silent crash / blank window.

Like others in this thread, my first instinct was to check the GPU because the logs kept pointing to:
`Child process crashed (type: 'GPU', exitCode: -2147483645)` followed by `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`

Turns out the GPU is a complete red herring (my Radeon 760M / drivers are totally fine). The exit code `-2147483645` is actually `0x80000003` (`STATUS_BREAKPOINT`). On recent Windows 11 builds with VBS/HVCI on, Chromium's sandbox trips up on child process initialization, crashes 5 times, and Chromium then gives up and blames the GPU process.

However, just passing `--no-sandbox` wasn't enough on its own—the app opened to a blank/invisible window. After digging into `app.asar`, I found the real blocker:

In the root `package.json`, `"type": "module"` is set. But `out/preload/index.js` was compiled using CommonJS (`require("electron")`). Because of the ESM declaration, Node throws:
`ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope`

This kills the preload bridge before `window.electron` gets exposed, so the frontend hangs, `ready-to-show` never triggers, and the window stays hidden forever.

Here is the quick patch that got it running 100% for me:

1. Unpacked `resources/app.asar` using `npx asar extract app.asar app_extracted`.
2. Created an `out/preload/package.json` with `{ "type": "commonjs" }` and renamed/copied `index.js` to `index.cjs`.
3. Updated `out/main/index.js` to point the preload to `../preload/index.cjs` and added `app.commandLine.appendSwitch("no-sandbox")` at the start of `index.js`.
4. Repacked the asar (`npx asar pack app_extracted app.asar`).

After repacking, the app launches instantly with full hardware acceleration enabled and no issues opening or closing.

Hope this helps anyone stuck on this, and hopefully the team can adjust the preload build target (e.g. outputting `.cjs` or scoping its package.json) in the next release!

## Workaround: musl binary + patchelf

The `cannot execute: required file not found` error happens because the official binary is linked against glibc, which Termux (bionic) does not ship.

**Working fix** — reuse upstreams musl-linked ARM64 binary with Alpine musl loader:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl/master/install.sh | sh
```

This:
1. Downloads the upstream `opencode-linux-arm64-musl.tar.gz`
2. Installs Alpine musl loader (`ld-musl-aarch64.so.1`) + `libstdc++`/`libgcc_s`
3. Patches the binary interpreter with `patchelf`
4. Builds `libresolvefix.so` (LD_PRELOAD shim for DNS on Android)
5. Installs a Python HTTP proxy (Bun io_uring is broken on Android)
6. Installs a wrapper that sets up the environment

After install, `opencode` works.

### Why a proxy?

Bun uses io_uring for networking. On Android, io_uring is broken — all outbound connections fail. The proxy routes traffic through Python using standard libc sockets. Adds ~100-200ms per request.

### OpenCode v2

v2 replaces Bun with Node.js. The v2 musl binary works on Termux natively — no proxy needed.

**Recommended install** — npm, then the wrapper-fix script (fixes the recursive self-call wrapper bug, patches the ELF interpreter, installs the musl binary package):

```sh
npm install -g @opencode-ai/cli@beta --force
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl/master/scripts/fix-opencode2-wrapper.sh | sh
```

Alternative: run v2 inside proot Ubuntu via `oc2-ubuntu` — see the [repo README](https://github.com/DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl#opencode-v2-beta).

<details>
<summary>Manual postinstall patch (fallback if the script doesn't fit your setup)</summary>

Patch `postinstall.mjs` (`$PREFIX/lib/node_modules/@opencode-ai/cli/postinstall.mjs`):

1. Add `android: "linux"` to the platform map (around line 16):
```js
// Before:
const platform = { darwin: "darwin", linux: "linux", win32: "windows" }[os.platform()] ?? os.platform()
// After:
const platform = { darwin: "darwin", linux: "linux", win32: "windows", android: "linux" }[os.platform()] ?? os.platform()
```

2. Force `isMusl()=true` on Android:
```js
function isMusl() {
  if (platform !== "linux") return false
  try {
    if (os.platform() === "android") return true  // ← add this line
    if (fs.existsSync("/etc/alpine-release")) return true
    // ...
```

Then manually install the musl binary:
```sh
npm install --ignore-scripts --no-save --force @opencode-ai/cli-linux-arm64-musl@beta
patchelf --set-interpreter "$PREFIX/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1" \
  "$PREFIX/lib/node_modules/@opencode-ai/cli-linux-arm64-musl/bin/opencode2"
cp "$PREFIX/lib/node_modules/@opencode-ai/cli-linux-arm64-musl/bin/opencode2" \
   "$PREFIX/lib/node_modules/@opencode-ai/cli/bin/opencode2"
```

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> `--force` is required because `android` is not in the npm packages supported OS list yet. Tracked in [#47612](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47612).
